title: Reduce GPU memory and workspace usage: selective activation-checkpointing, arena tuner, scratch buffer reuse
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory usage for large models by ~20-35% through selective activation checkpointing, arena allocator tuning, and scratch buffer reuse. Improved 99th-percentile latency under sustained continuous-batching load by ~7% and reduced OOMs in constrained devices. No API changes.
description: Context: In multi-tenant and Dedicated deployments we still see GPU OOMs and large workspace allocations under continuous batching and long-context workloads. This PR reduces peak GPU workspace/memory pressure by combining three complementary techniques: (1) selective activation checkpointing that checkpoints only high-cost blocks instead of blanket checkpointing, (2) an arena allocator tuning and scratch buffer reuse strategy to avoid repeated large temporary allocations, and (3) conservative workspace accounting in the continuous-batcher so we allocate a single shared workspace sized for the batch instead of per-request worst-case. Changes are safe by default and opt-in controls are provided for legacy behavior. Summary of changes: selective checkpointing algorithm added and integrated with kernel selector so kernels that support recompute use smaller activation footprints; arena allocator introduces growth thresholds, per-device max_scratch_size, and a sub-allocation free-list to reuse scratch buffers between kernels; continuous batcher now computes aggregated workspace requirement and requests a single arena allocation per batch; KV cache eviction threshold reduced slightly to free transient space under memory pressure and avoid aggressive expansion; small kernel variants selected when workspace-constrained. Benchmarks and results: microbench on 13B decoder-only model, seq_len=4096, batch=8: peak GPU memory reduced ~28% (from 32.1GB to 23.1GB). End-to-end throughput sustained within 3% of baseline; 99th percentile latency improved ~7% under a sustained continuous-batching scenario. On smaller GPUs (A10G-like 24GB) this change eliminated intermittent OOMs in our perf-canary runs. CI and rollout: unit and integration tests added; perf regression jobs and a canary rollout were executed in staging. Risk and config: defaults are conservative; operators can disable selective checkpointing or set arena max_scratch_size via runtime config. Checklist: [x] tests added and passing, [x] perf benchmarks captured, [x] docs/notes added (docs/perf/arena_tuning.md), [x] Linear tickets referenced. Motivation and rationale: avoids large per-request transient allocations that dominate peak usage and cause OOMs while keeping throughput intact. Related work: follows up on ENG-1123 and earlier arena tuning experiments in perf-canary.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice set of changes, can you quantify how the checkpoint_threshold was chosen? Are there workloads where we regress quality or CPU usage?

Aisha Patel (author): checkpoint_threshold is tuned using per-block activation profiling we run during model onboarding; default chosen to cover top 20% activation contributors which reduces memory most of the time with <2% extra compute. We added a runtime flag to override and a Linear task to further tune per-model thresholds.
